title: Senior Industrial Designer | Robotics
description:
Your tasks

  • Shape the hardware identity: Define how our humanoids look and feel: proportions, surfaces, overall silhouette. You take the design direction we already have and carry it through to physical systems that actually ship.
  • Design for passive safety first: Safety sits in the geometry from the first sketch. You work through clearances, pinch points, contact surfaces and fall behavior so the robot is safe around people before software gets involved.
  • Integrate complex systems: Package the internals (sensors, cameras, cooling, connectors, cable routing) so the technical parts look intended.
  • Physical human machine interaction: Design status signals, touchpoints and small physical cues that tell the people working next to the robot what it is doing and what comes next.
  • Build the ecosystem around the robot: Extend the design language to charging docks, transport cases, maintenance gear and packaging.
  • From model to CAD: You build physical models fast, see what holds up, and change them until they do. Then you do the surfacing and hand over CAD that engineering can build from directly.
  • Materials and processes: Select finishes, review physical samples, and work suppliers on feasibility, cost and lead times. You are willing to try materials that are not standard and to bring in specialized external labs.


Your profile

  • Background: A degree in industrial or product design, or an engineering degree where the design side is clearly the stronger half.
  • Experience: Around five years or more designing physical products, in house or at a studio. Robotics, medical devices, lab and industrial equipment, mobility, or another field where the hardware has to hold up in front of people.
  • Small series: You have worked on products built in the hundreds rather than the millions, and know how much that changes what a shape can be.
  • Safety and regulation: You have designed under mechanical safety requirements before, so guarding, clearances and contact safety are familiar territory rather than a new topic.
  • Tools: Surface modeling in Rhino, Onshape, SolidWorks or Fusion, plus 3D printing and enough workshop practice to build your own models.
  • Working with engineers: You read mechanical drawings, keep up in technical discussions, and can explain why a design decision matters.
  • Languages: Fluent English. German is nice to have, not a requirement.


Why us?

  • Ownership from day one: The physical design and hardware identity of our humanoids is yours. Short decisions, no approval chains, and you work directly with the founders and lead engineers.
  • Everything under one roof: Labs, workshop and test rigs are in the same Kreuzberg building. The engineer you need is a walk away, not a ticket.
  • Room to get better: Paid learning time and a personal budget for it, projects where something is allowed to not work the first time, and support for portfolio work and conference talks as the company becomes known.
  • Benefits: A benefits package you put together yourself, covering mobility, home setup, health or food. Plus one extra paid day off a year for volunteering or a project you care about.

How to Apply

Send us your portfolio and a few lines about one product you took from sketch to production: what changed along the way, and why. No cover letter needed.

Process: Intro call -> Portfolio deep-dive with the founders -> Half-day on-site visit with a small design exercise -> Offer.

We build robots for everyone, so we want a team that reflects that. We hire on what you can do, and we welcome applications from people who are underrepresented in hardware design. If you don't tick every box but think this is your job, apply anyway.

description:

Deine Aufgaben

Deine Kernaufgaben sind:

  • Strategische Projekte leiten: Du leitest eigenverantwortlich bereichsübergreifende Veränderungs-, Effizienz- und Prozessoptimierungsprojekte sowie Software- und Digitalisierungsprojekte.
  • Agile Softwareprojekte steuern: Du arbeitest eng mit Fachbereichen und Entwicklungsteams zusammen, koordinierst Prioritäten und Abhängigkeiten und hilfst, die agile Zusammenarbeit weiter auszubauen.
  • Komplexität in umsetzbare Pläne übersetzen: Du klärst Ziele und Umfang, strukturierst Arbeitspakete und steuerst Meilensteine, Zeit, Ressourcen, Budgets, Risiken und Abhängigkeiten: klassisch, agil oder hybrid.
  • Entscheidungen vorbereiten und vertreten: Du erstellst entscheidungsreife Management-Updates und Steering-Unterlagen mit Empfehlungen, Szenarien und klaren Entscheidungsbedarfen. Projektergebnisse und Zielkonflikte vertrittst du souverän gegenüber Stakeholdern und Führungskräften.
  • Teams zusammenbringen: Du führst interdisziplinäre Projektteams lateral und moderierst Workshops und Entscheidungsprozesse – dabei bringst du unterschiedliche Perspektiven und Prioritäten zusammen.
  • Energiewirtschaftliche Projekte voranbringen: Du arbeitest dich in die relevanten Zusammenhänge im Umfeld von Energiehandel, Direktvermarktung und digitalen Lösungen ein, stellst die richtigen Fragen und führst fachliche, technische und operative Anforderungen zu belastbaren Lösungen und konkreten Projektergebnissen zusammen.
  • End-to-End-Prozesse verbessern: Du analysierst Abläufe, erkennst Brüche und Verbesserungspotenziale und gestaltest wirksame, effiziente Prozesse mit klaren Verantwortlichkeiten und pragmatischen Lösungen.
  • Budgetcontrolling: Du prüfst projektbezogene Stunden und Kosten, koordinierst die Rechnungsfreigabe und behältst das Projektbudget im Blick.

Darüber hinaus gestaltest du unser Projektmanagement weiter:

  • Verbesserungen wirklich umsetzen: Du treibst die gemeinsam identifizierten und beschlossenen Effizienz- und Prozessverbesserungen voran und überprüfst, ob die angestrebte Wirkung im Alltag eintritt.
  • Projektmanagement weiterentwickeln: Du entwickelst Methoden, Frameworks und Best-Practices weiter, besonders für agile Softwareentwicklungsprojekte, und stärkst damit Qualität, Tempo und Ergebnisorientierung.
  • Projektarbeit bereichsübergreifend verankern: Du bindest die relevanten Fachbereiche ein, integrierst die Projektarbeit in den laufenden Geschäftsbetrieb und sorgst für klare Verantwortlichkeiten, verbindliche Entscheidungen und sichtbare Fortschritte. In einer Organisation mit dezentralen Zuständigkeiten entwickelst du unsere Projektmanagement-Strukturen, Rollen und Standards pragmatisch weiter.


Dein Profil

Das bringst du mit:

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der eigenständigen Leitung komplexer Projekte, idealerweise in Veränderungsprojekten, Prozessoptimierung, Digitalisierung oder Softwareentwicklung.
  • Fundierte Praxis im klassischen Projektmanagement, zum Beispiel in Planung und Steuerung von Umfang, Terminen, Ressourcen, Risiken und Abhängigkeiten.
  • Vor allem bringst du praktische Erfahrung im agilen Projektmanagement von Softwareentwicklungsprojekten mit und hast idealerweise bereits KI-gestützte Werkzeuge oder Methoden im Projektkontext eingesetzt.

  • Klare Kommunikation, analytisches und strukturiertes Denken sowie die Fähigkeit, auch bei unterschiedlichen Perspektiven und Prioritäten Orientierung zu schaffen.
  • Sicherheit in der Moderation von Workshops und in der lateralen Führung interdisziplinärer Teams.
  • Interesse daran, Projektmanagement-Strukturen, Rollen und Standards weiterzuentwickeln. Du bringst Eigeninitiative, Pragmatismus und den Anspruch mit, Konzepte nicht nur zu entwickeln, sondern Ergebnisse gemeinsam mit den Beteiligten in die Praxis zu bringen.
  • Ein abgeschlossenes Studium oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation. Entscheidend ist für uns vor allem deine relevante Projekterfahrung.
  • Erfahrung in der Modellierung und Dokumentation von Geschäftsprozessen mit BPMN sowie deren Anwendung im Projektmanagement. 
  • Energiewirtschaftliche Erfahrung ist ein Plus, aber keine Voraussetzung. Hilfreich sind Kenntnisse zu erneuerbaren Energien, Direktvermarktung, Stromhandel, Bilanzkreismanagement, PPAs oder virtuellen Kraftwerken. Du solltest jedoch bereit und in der Lage sein, dich zügig in energiewirtschaftliche Zusammenhänge einzuarbeiten, fachliche Anforderungen zu verstehen und gemeinsam mit den Teams in tragfähige Lösungen und umsetzbare Arbeitspakete zu übersetzen.

title: Senior Sales Manager UK
description:
Our project for you:

moebel.de is Europe's leading price comparison site for furniture and home furnishings. Our family of portals operates in nine European countries, including Germany, France, Spain, the Netherlands, Italy and Poland.

Now we are getting started in earnest in the UK: living24.uk is live – our price comparison site for furniture, home furnishings, garden and décor, as well as white goods and home electronics. The launch is done, the technology works. What decides the pace now are the retailers: the more relevant shops list their ranges on living24.uk, the stronger the comparison for users – and the faster the portal grows.

This is not selling from a tidy list of existing accounts. You take on a freshly launched market and build the partner portfolio that living24.uk runs on. Whoever delivers over the next few months will shape what moebel.de looks like in the UK.

That is why we are looking for you as Senior Sales Manager UK.


Your future Tasks

  • Building the market: you build living24.uk's partner portfolio – from first contact through pitch and negotiation to the signed contract. Your targets are UK online retailers in furniture, home furnishings, garden, décor, white goods, home electronics and small appliances.
  • Selling a performance model: you show retailers how living24.uk pays off as an additional channel – through cost per click, visibility, feed quality and cost-of-sale.
  • Seeing partners through to go-live: product feed, tracking, range checks – together with the team in Hamburg. After go-live our Relationship Management team takes over day-to-day care, so you can focus on winning new partners.
  • Presence in the market: retailer visits, trade fairs and industry events across the UK. In a young market, trust is built face to face.
  • Ear to the ground: competition, price levels, what UK retailers expect, seasonality – what you learn in the field feeds into product, pricing and priorities.


Your Strenghts

  • Several years of sales experience in UK e-commerce, ideally with a price comparison site, marketplace, affiliate network or performance marketing provider
  • A solid network of UK retailers in our categories that you can put to work from day one
  • Command of the performance model: CPC, CPO, affiliate, product feeds, ROAS and cost-of-sale are selling points for you, not buzzwords
  • A hunter's mindset: you keep your own pipeline full, cold outreach included, and get deals over the line
  • An appetite for building: pace and open questions appeal to you more than a field that has already been ploughed
  • Working from the numbers, with clean CRM records as the basis for how you steer
  • Willingness to travel across the UK and to regular meetings in Hamburg
  • Fluent English at negotiation level – German is a plus, not a requirement


Our Benefits

Your day is yours to shape

Work when you are most productive. Early bird or night owl: you set your hours flexibly, in agreement with your team. Working from another European country for a while? No problem. Your laptop is your workplace.

Our culture is one of a kind

Here everyone sits on the same couch, regardless of title or role. We live team spirit online and in person – gaming nights, workouts, film evenings and team events.

Four times a year we meet for Company Week

Working together in the office, pushing projects forward, pizza evenings and a party to finish.

In the heart of Hamburg

When you are in Hamburg, our office is waiting for you – centrally located between the main station, Mönckebergstraße and the Binnenalster lake. Perfect for lunch dates, a break by the Alster or a stroll after work.


We are looking forward to receiving your application!

Please send your application exclusively through our online application form – it goes straight to our recruiting team. You are welcome to submit your CV in English or German, ideally with your salary expectations and earliest possible start date.

Supply, Manage, Flex – kombiniert. Diese Integration ermöglicht Einsparungen von bis zu 30 % bei den wiederkehrenden Stromkosten und unterstützt Unternehmen gleichzeitig dabei, auf erneuerbare Energien umzusteigen.

Wir sind Europas am schnellsten wachsende B2B-Energieplattform. Aktuell sind wir in Deutschland und Österreich aktiv und planen, unsere Aktivitäten 2027 auf einen dritten Markt auszuweiten. Unser Ziel ist die europaweite Skalierung. Wir bewegen uns schnell – das Marktfenster ist offen, und wir wollen es nutzen.

Über trawa

trawa ist ein Scale-up mit Sitz in Berlin und rund 100 Mitarbeitenden, davon etwa 30 in Product & Tech. Bis heute haben wir mehr als 35 Millionen Euro eingesammelt, darunter eine Series-A-Finanzierungsrunde über 24 Millionen Euro im Mai 2025. Zu unseren Investoren zählen Balderton, Headline, Speedinvest, AENU, Magnetic und Tiny VC.

Wir suchen eine:n Account Executive, um gemeinsam die nächste Wachstumsstufe zu erreichen. Du berichtest an unseren Head of Sales und arbeitest eng mit unseren Commercial-Teams zusammen.

Die Position ist in Berlin angesiedelt. trawa ist ein Office-First-Unternehmen: In der Regel arbeitest du an fünf Tagen pro Woche aus unserem Büro.

Das Team

Unser Sales Team ist ein zentraler Bestandteil für den kommerziellen Erfolg von trawa. Vom Erstkontakt mit einem Lead bis zum erfolgreichem Abschluss mit einem Kunden, berät das Team mittelständische Unternehmen zu unseren ganzheitlichen Energielösungen.

Wen wir suchen

  • Ermögliche signifikante Stromkosteneinsparungen bei unseren Kunden durch gezielte Positionierung unserer Lösungen zur intelligenten Stromversorgung und Steuerung von Batteriespeichern

Deine Ziele in den ersten 90 Tagen

  • Erfahrungen in der B2B-Kundenkommunikation, z. B. als Account Executive, Account Manager oder im Business Development Bereich

  • Erfahrung in der Energiewirtschaft bzw. Erneuerbare Energien ist ein großes Plus, aber kein Muss

  • Abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium (mindestens Bachelor)

  • Ausgeprägte Überzeugungskraft und ein sicheres Gespür für Gesprächssituationen

  • Interesse an energiewirtschaftlichen Lösungen und intrinsische Motivation, die Energiewende aktiv mitzugestalten

  • Starkes Organisationstalent und Fähigkeit, Prioritäten in einem dynamischen Arbeitsumfeld zu setzen

  • Exzellente Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

Warum trawa?

Wirkung: Europäische KMU geben jährlich zwischen 150.000 und 10 Millionen Euro für Strom aus – viele davon zahlen zu viel und sind an veraltete Beschaffungsmodelle gebunden. Mit unserem Produkt veränderst du unmittelbar, wie Tausende Unternehmen Energie einkaufen, managen und nutzen. Die Wirkung ist messbar, der Markt ist riesig und der Zeitpunkt ist jetzt.

Verantwortung: Bei uns übernimmst du Verantwortung für deine Themen und treibst Ergebnisse voran – unabhängig von deinem Hintergrund oder deiner bisherigen Berufserfahrung.

Lernen und Entwicklung: Wir stellen dir ein jährliches Weiterbildungsbudget und feste Zeit für deine persönliche und fachliche Entwicklung zur Verfügung. Dich erwarten Mentoring, vielfältige Lernmöglichkeiten und echte Perspektiven für deinen nächsten Karriereschritt.

Vielfalt und Inklusion: Wir sind ein Arbeitgeber, der Chancengleichheit lebt, und unser Team spiegelt das wider. Menschen aus mehr als 15 Nationen bringen unterschiedliche Sprachen, Erfahrungen und Perspektiven zusammen. Bei trawa ist Familienfreundlichkeit auf allen Ebenen selbstverständlich – in unserem Team und in der Führung arbeiten Eltern. Wir setzen uns für ein inklusives Umfeld ein, in dem alle ihr Bestes geben können.

Vergütung und Benefits: Wir bieten ein wettbewerbsfähiges Vergütungspaket mit Gehalt und Stock Options, 30 Urlaubstagen sowie zahlreichen Benefits. Bei trawa bauen wir einen vielfältigen, inklusiven und authentischen Arbeitsplatz auf. Wenn dich die Position begeistert, dein bisheriger Weg aber nicht in allen Punkten dem Anforderungsprofil entspricht, freuen wir uns trotzdem über deine Bewerbung. title: Expansion Intern | Austria or Netherlands
description:
Expansion Intern | Austria or Netherlands

Internship · Full-time · Berlin (HQ)

 

Our mission for you

Take trawa beyond borders!

As an Expansion Intern, you'll play a key role in taking trawa into new markets and will experience hands-on what it means to be an operator. You'll work across go-to-market, operations and product, and see up close what it takes to bring a fast-growing energy platform into a new country. We are hiring on a rolling basis, minimum duration is 3 months.

Two markets, one mission:

  • Austria: trawa is already live here, and you'll help scale the market: speeding up growth, sharpening our local positioning and turning our Austrian presence into a success story.

  • The Netherlands: trawa is preparing its Dutch market entry, and you'll help lay the foundations from day one: understanding the market, positioning trawa, supporting our first sales and commercial activities, and preparing everything for launch.

We staff you on the market where your profile and our needs fit best. Either way, you'll build something that truly matters.

 
 

What you'll do, whichever market you work on:

  • Supercharge local go-to-market: You research competitors, help define how trawa wins in your market and support early customer acquisition. Your work directly drives our local growth.

  • Turn regulation into a competitive edge: Energy markets change constantly. You track legal and regulatory updates, work out what they mean for trawa and help us adapt faster than anyone else.

  • Build local operations: You support product rollouts, from contract frameworks to processes, and help adapt what works at our Berlin HQ to the local market.

  • Shape the product for new markets: You bring local customer and market insights into our product team and help make sure trawa fits the needs of businesses in your country.

  • Become the market expert: You run ad-hoc analyses, build market overviews and quickly become the go-to person for everything specific to your country.

  • Collaborate with leadership: You work closely with our expansion leads and senior leadership. You take ownership of your own initiatives and see them through from idea to execution.

  • You are a true team player: You understand that humility and performance go hand in hand, and that what counts is the overall success of the team.

 

Who we are looking for

Standout candidates who want to grow with us:

  • Advanced Bachelor's student, in your gap year, Master's student, or recent graduate with outstanding academic achievements.

  • You have a strong track record. Analytical skills, an entrepreneurial mindset and a high degree of independence set you apart.

  • You’re highly motivated, hands-on, and eager to take real responsibility.

  • You have first practical experience in a dynamic startup, top-tier strategy consultancy or investment banking.

  • You're curious about the energy transition and are not scared of legal texts.

Market-specific requirements:

  • Austrian team: You are fluent in English and German (C1 or higher), and you're based in or willing to move to Berlin.

  • Dutch team: You are fluent in English, German and Dutch are a plus, and you're based in or willing to move to Amsterdam.

 

Why us?

  • Your impact: Your work has a direct influence on how trawa grows across Europe, and you get to help shape a new market from the ground up.

  • Flexible working: We foster a vibrant company culture where we love to work together, and home office is also an option. With flexible working hours and 30 vacation days, we support your work-life balance.

  • Attractive benefits: In addition to a competitive salary, you'll receive lunch vouchers, a learning and development budget and an Urban Sports Club membership.

  • Diversity & inclusion: Everyone is welcome at trawa! We are committed to an inclusive workplace that values diversity. We actively encourage people of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnic backgrounds, and physical or neurodiverse abilities to apply.

  • Application process: You'll receive feedback within a week. The process includes interviews, a practical challenge and conversations with our team.

Don't worry if you don't meet every single requirement. If you're excited about the role and our mission, we want to hear from you!

 

About us

trawa is a fast-growing energy start-up that is revolutionizing the way businesses procure and manage their energy consumption and costs. Our mission is to make sustainable energy accessible and affordable for every business. We are seeking talented individuals who are passionate about making a positive impact and contributing to our shared success.

title: Head of Operational Integration
description:
About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials for energy, infrastructure, and construction in wholesale and beyond.

We trade with global suppliers and distribute to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade and distribution end-to-end: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, and embedded financing. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier; for our partners, it is the most convenient and safe way to do business across borders. Behind it, our software and agentic AI do the heavy lifting that used to take an asset-intensive supply chain with four or five intermediaries and weeks of manual coordination.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover

  • Seven European markets live

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), offices in London, Mumbai, and Shanghai

$40M Series B just closed, $75M raised to date from Atomico, Project A, and Inven Capital, institutional financing from international banks.

We are building the world's first and last industrial-grade AI operating system for materials, redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

Acquisitions are our second growth path. We buy established industrial distribution businesses in the EUR 20-40M revenue range, owners and management stay on board, and we connect them to our platform, our procurement, our financing lines and our AI stack. Three deals are live, two are close to signature, and at run rate we intend to close around five per year out of a mapped universe of roughly 200 targets.

Role Overview

You own what happens after signing.

Origination, valuation and deal execution sit with the CEO and our senior M&A advisor. Your mandate starts the day a company becomes part of Andercore and it ends when that company runs better than it did before.

These are analog businesses. Fifteen years old, owner-led, hemdsärmelig, a well-run P&L and almost no technology underneath it. They are profitable, they are growing, and they are at their operational limit. Our hypothesis is that our platform, our purchasing power, our credit facilities and our automation take them past that limit. Your job is to find out on the ground whether that hypothesis holds, in which order, and at what pace - and then to make it happen with the management team, not to them.

We do not arrive as the saviour with the AI magic box. We say so explicitly to every seller, and you will hold that line.

What You Will Own

Holding Management from Day 1

  • Access to accounting and financials from day one, monthly numbers on a fixed close, one reporting framework across all acquired entities.

  • Set the baseline: revenue, margin, working capital, cash, customer and supplier concentration. No opinion without the number behind it.

  • Pick up the commitments made during due diligence and turn them into the operating rhythm of the first 100 days.

  • Run the portfolio as a financial participation first. Both companies are growing. Do not put anything into a skid.

On-the-Ground Diagnosis

  • Spend real time inside the acquired businesses and find out where they actually stand, which is never where they say they stand.

  • Map the connection points: procurement, pricing, inventory, sales productivity, logistics, financing, ERP, reporting.

  • Test our integration theses against reality, quantify the ones that hold, kill the ones that do not, and bring the correction back to the CEO fast.

Value Creation

  • Sequence and land the levers with the management team: central procurement, our credit and working-capital facilities, pricing, sales productivity, customer intelligence, automation of manual back office.

  • Decide with the CEO what gets centralized, what stays entrepreneurial, and what we take from them - the flow runs in both directions, several of these companies do things better than we do.

  • Track every lever against the original investment case in euros.

Owner and Management Relationship

  • Be the peer of a Geschäftsführer who built a EUR 30M business himself. Credibility comes from having done operating work, not from a framework.

  • Be the one who checks whether things are as good as they are described, and who says it out loud when they are not. The CEO stays the partner; you bring the uncomfortable version.

  • Manage expectations in the other direction too: we are not a service provider that solves the acquired company's problems for it.

Playbook and Team

  • Codify integration into a repeatable capability: Day-1 checklist, reporting standard, diagnostic framework, lever library, 100-day plan.

  • Make the fourth acquisition faster than the first, then build and lead the team that runs them in parallel.

Scope Boundaries / What This Role Is Not

  • Not M&A. No origination, no valuation, no LOI, no SPA. That sits with the CEO and our senior M&A advisor.

  • Not a PMO. Nobody here sends a 400-line integration plan with traffic lights to an owner-manager. That gets you thrown out of the room, correctly.

  • Not a consulting engagement. You are measured on the numbers of the acquired companies, not on the quality of the analysis.

  • Not a corporate integration role. These are not hierarchical organizations that execute what the centre decides.

  • Not a process you inherit. There is none yet. You build it.

What We Are Looking For

You are an operator out of a private equity value-creation or portfolio operations team, or a generalist from strategy and transformation with real time spent inside operating companies. Roughly eight to twelve years in.

You bring:

  • At least one integration or post-close situation you personally carried, where you can name the specific knotty problem you solved and why it worked. We will ask for that story in the first interview.

  • Operating substance: you have sat in procurement, pricing, supply chain, finance or sales of a real company, not only next to it.

  • Geländegängigkeit. You are comfortable with an entrepreneur who is highly intelligent, rough around the edges, and holds two cars and a boat inside the company. Nothing about that scenario throws you.

  • People work as roughly half the job. Influence without formal authority, because these managing directors did not sign up to be managed.

  • A strong observer. You read a business and a person quickly and accurately.

  • Fluent German and English. German is not optional; these conversations happen in German.

  • Fluency with modern AI tooling and the instinct to automate your own work. You do not need to be an engineer.

You do not need five PMI programmes on your CV. We would rather you had none than that you learned to fill in lists instead of thinking.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 12 months:

  • Every acquired entity reports monthly on one framework, on a fixed close, with us having access to accounting.

  • Each acquisition has its integration thesis validated or killed with numbers within 90 days of closing.

  • The acquired businesses keep growing. No customer, supplier or key person lost to the transaction.

  • The first value-creation levers are live and their P&L impact is measurable in euros.

  • A documented playbook exists, and the next integration starts faster than the last.

Over time you own integration and value creation for the whole group at a pace of several acquisitions per year, and build the team that delivers it.

Package

  • Fixed base plus a variable component tied directly to the success of each integration.

  • Virtual equity in Andercore at the current strike, with meaningful upside if we build what we intend to build.

  • Direct work with the Founder & CEO, the M&A advisor, the Board and our investors.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or any other characteristic.

  • Seven European markets live

We are building the world's first and last industrial-grade AI operating system for materials, redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

Role Overview

As VP Engineering, you own the Engineering organization and turn our platform and AI vision into shipped systems. You report to the Chief Product Officer and partner closely with product, commercial, operations, and finance. You lead our Senior Product Engineers, Staff Engineers and QA, and work closely with our product managers, who own product and design.

This is an execution mandate. You carve our core systems into a modern platform, build our AI agents into one holistic system that runs the trade lifecycle end-to-end, and scale the teams that deliver it. You inherit a working machine at full speed: your job is to rebuild it in flight without losing a day of momentum. In your first year, the priorities are the carve-out of our transaction core and bringing our AI agents into one orchestrating layer.

Key Responsibilities

AI and Automation

  • Build our AI agents into one holistic, orchestrating AI layer across sourcing, pricing, quoting, sales, logistics, and financing.

  • Drive automation of the full transaction lifecycle, and own automation-rate and no-touch-quote targets as first-class delivery KPIs.

  • Work with our data team, which sits with the CPO, on systems that make our trade flows a compounding advantage, so every transaction makes the system smarter.

  • Keep us at the practical frontier of agentic AI: ship what creates leverage now, skip what is demo-ware.

  • Put the guardrails, evals, and human-in-the-loop controls in place so automation stays reliable where it matters most: money-touching and customer-facing paths, where a wrong output is a real loss, not just a bug.

Platform and Architecture

  • Own execution of the target architecture for the Andercore platform, the system of record for industrial trade.

  • Lead the carve-out of our transaction core into a modern, modular light ERP (a lean core system for our trade transactions), with a clear migration path and zero disruption to daily trading.

  • Shape the role of Salesforce in our landscape: decide what stays on the platform, what moves to the new core, and how the two work together.

ÜBERNIMM VERANTWORTUNG, WO LEISTUNG ENTSTEHT

Du hast bereits Verantwortung in Produktion, Industrie, Logistik oder einem vergleichbaren operativen Umfeld übernommen und möchtest Teams nicht nur verwalten, sondern aktiv weiterentwickeln?

Dann werde Teil unseres Teams als Projektleiter (m/w/d).

Du übernimmst die operative Verantwortung für ein Kundenprojekt im logistischen Umfeld. Dabei sorgst du für stabile Abläufe, eine verlässliche Personalplanung sowie die Erreichung von Qualitäts-, Produktivitäts- und Leistungszielen.

Du bist die zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen Mitarbeitenden, Kundenansprechpartnern und Geschäftsführung – mit dem Anspruch, Herausforderungen nicht nur zu melden, sondern nachhaltig zu lösen.

  • Du übernimmst die operative Führung eines Logistikteams bei einem unserer Kundenprojekte.

  • Du steuerst Personal-, Einsatz- und Kapazitätsplanung und stellst eine verlässliche Projektbesetzung sicher.

  • Du reagierst souverän auf Abweichungen, Engpässe und kurzfristige operative Herausforderungen.

  • Du dokumentierst Leistungen, Entwicklungen und relevante Abweichungen nachvollziehbar.

  • Du bist regelmäßig auf der Fläche präsent und gehst als Führungskraft voran.

DAS BRINGST DU MIT

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung in einer Führungsfunktion in Produktion, Industrie, Metallverarbeitung, Gießerei, Logistik oder einem vergleichbaren Umfeld.

  • Erfahrung als Produktionsleiter, Projektleiter, Teamleiter, Lagerleiter, Schichtleiter, Vorarbeiter oder Gruppenleiter.

  • Gute Kenntnisse in der Steuerung von Produktionsabläufen, Personalplanung und operativen Kennzahlen.

  • Ein gutes Gespür für Menschen sowie die Fähigkeit, Teams verbindlich, fair und klar zu führen.

  • Eine strukturierte, pragmatische und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise.

  • Durchsetzungsstärke, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und eine ausgeprägte Hands-on-Mentalität.

  • Führerschein Klasse B.

  • Projektbezogene Reisebereitschaft.

WARUM DIESE POSITION?

Diese Rolle ist für Menschen, die operative Führung ernst nehmen. Du gestaltest nicht aus der Distanz, sondern direkt dort, wo Leistung entsteht.

Du hast sichtbaren Einfluss auf Abläufe, Qualität, Produktivität und die Entwicklung deines Teams. Gleichzeitig arbeitest du eng mit unseren Kunden und der Geschäftsführung zusammen und kannst Prozesse aktiv weiterentwickeln.

KLINGT NACH DIR?

Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung, wenn du die genannten Muss-Kriterien erfüllst und bereit bist, bundesweit Verantwortung in unseren Kundenprojekten zu übernehmen.

Sende deine Bewerbungsunterlagen einfach über unser Bewerbungsformular oder per E-Mail an

DEIN KONTAKT BEI FRAGEN

Tarsi, Krisztian
+49 1515 2591381

ÜBER DIE TABEL GRUPPE

Die TABEL Gruppe ist ein führendes Dienstleistungsunternehmen im Bereich Business Process Outsourcing im fertigungsnahen Umfeld.

Von der Prozessanalyse über die Projektkonzeption bis zur Umsetzung und Begleitung steht das Erreichen der Produktivitätsziele unserer Kunden im Mittelpunkt unseres Handelns.

Mit rund 3.000 Mitarbeitenden an über 30 Standorten unterstützen wir unsere Kunden dabei, Kosten zu senken, ihre Wettbewerbsfähigkeit zu stärken und sich auf ihre Kernkompetenzen zu konzentrieren. title: (Senior) Technical Partnerships Manager  - Corporate Travel (all genders)
description:
Distribusion is the world’s leading ground transportation marketplace and gives travelers seamless access to ground transportation online, from search to ticket purchase. We have built a cutting-edge B2B technology platform that connects bus, rail, and ferry operators in 70+ countries with the biggest online retailers, including Google Maps and Booking.com.
We are shaping the future of travel and building the largest global network of transport providers and retailers. We are one of the fastest growing startups in travel, backed by leading VCs (TQ Ventures, Lightrock, Creandum and Northzone), and now, following our recent $80m Series C funding, we are ready to push beyond.

Distribusion is quickly expanding globally and looking for a (Senior) Technical Partnerships Manager to join the Corporate Travel Partnerships team to drive the strategic growth and performance of some of our key partnerships in the business travel space. This role will require you to wear many hats and certainly not leave you bored!

What you will do:

  • Support Pre-Sales: Act as a technical expert during initial engagements to evaluate partner needs and demonstrate our capabilities.

  • Consult on API Implementation: Guide partners through their API integration, ensuring a seamless process that meets certification standards.

  • Translate Requirements: Gather technical requirements directly from external partners and break them down into actionable specs for internal teams.

  • Manage Custom Projects: Drive the end-to-end delivery of custom developments, managing timelines, stakeholders, and go-live execution

  • Guide Product Development: Leverage partner feedback and insights to shape the ongoing development of our core API and integration tools.

  • Manage Technical Relationships: Own the long-term technical relationship with partners to drive collaboration, product engagement, and brand stickiness.

Workplace: We are mainly looking for this role based in Germany, preferably at our headquarters in Berlin.
We are a remote-first company, with teams around the Globe and our HQ office in Berlin, where the team often meets in the office.



Who you are:

  • 5 + years of work experience in a tech company (experience in a technology/software company, travel agency, transportation, and logistics industry is an advantage but not a must). 

  • You have had deep exposure to API integrations, and you are confident in navigating documentation, sprint cycles, and system architecture, even if you’re not the one coding.

  • A big plus if you have experience in the corporate travel space (any vertical).

  • You’re a structured communicator who can translate complexity into clarity for both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • You take ownership, thrive in ambiguity, and are energised by solving cross-functional coordination challenges.

  • You’re fluent in English, both written and spoken. Other languages are a plus.

  • You’re open to business travel, as needed.

What you can expect:

  • You will join a fast-paced travel tech company and take on a rapidly growing industry.

  • You will take on ownership and responsibility from day one and have a direct impact on the success of the company.

  • We value agility! We’re constantly updating our tech stack and offer the best possible tools to ensure all of our in-house engineers, partners, and carriers benefit from cutting-edge, efficient solutions.

  • You will work with global companies. Our product attracts the biggest names in travel technology, such as Booking.com, Google Maps, and national carriers like Amtrak, Deutsche Bahn, Renfe, and SNCF.

  • You will join an international team of talented and driven people with a clear mission. Expect your colleagues to inspire, support and challenge you every day!

  • We offer flexible and remote working conditions, relocation opportunities, and career growth in a small and developing company.

Your Talent Partner (TP) and point of contact is Masha Marynova, and the Hiring Manager (HM) is Sara Fahrenhorst.

title: Engineer - Data & Platforms (m/f/d)
description:
Your Role & How we work

As our Engineer - Data & Platforms (m/f/d), you build and run the internal data products that our investment team, Quantitative Research and AI Engineering rely on every day: the pipelines, datasets, APIs and tools that turn a large and growing pool of financial and alternative data into something investors can act on. Our stack is Python, SQL, AWS, and Databricks.

You report to our Director of Engineering. This is a hands-on engineering role: most of your time goes to designing, building, and shipping. The team is small, so you take ownership of real products early, and you get a manager and colleagues invested in your growth into investment and data-platform topics. You work closely with Quantitative Research, AI Engineering, Product & Data, and the investment team, and we treat agentic AI as a default in how we build.

What you will do

  • Build and improve the internal products the investment and research teams use daily: data pipelines, datasets, APIs, and tooling, on top of our lakehouse and orchestration stack.

  • Work directly with the teams you build for: take in their requests, triage and prioritise them, protect the integrity and consistency of the product, and explain features and implementation trade-offs in clear, non-technical language.

  • Design, build, and operate reliable data pipelines, ETLs and integrations that handle complex financial and alternative datasets.

  • Bring and reinforce good engineering habits in the team: automated testing at several levels, CI/CD, pull requests and code review, and clear documentation.

  • Contribute to operational excellence: observability, monitoring, data quality, and secure data handling.

  • Use agentic AI across engineering work (coding, review, testing, debugging, documentation) and help the team push these practices forward.


The experience you bring

  • 3 to 5 years of professional software or data engineering experience, building and operating systems in production.

  • Strong Python and strong SQL, with clean, readable code and a good sense for data modelling.

  • Proven engineering discipline: you write tests (unit, integration, data quality), work with CI/CD, and use pull requests and code review as a matter of course, and you can show how you helped a team adopt them.

  • Clear communication with non-engineers: you can explain what you built, why, and what it will and will not do, and you can say no constructively.

  • Hands-on use of AI across engineering functions, including frontier coding systems such as Claude Code and Codex, as a core part of how you work.

  • Genuine interest in investing, financial markets and data, and the ambition to grow into these topics.

  • Nice to have: Databricks or PySpark; data platform tooling such as orchestration (Airflow, Dagster or similar), lakehouse formats (Parquet, Delta, Iceberg) and AWS; experience with investment, financial or market data; building web frontends or APIs for internal tools; LLM systems in production.


2 reasons why you should not apply

  • You prefer fully specified tickets and no contact with users. Here the people you build for sit next to you, ask for things directly, and expect you to weigh in on what should be built and how.

  • You treat AI tooling as an occasional helper. We expect agentic AI to be a default in how you build, review, test, and ship, every day, not now and then.


Your mindset

  • You are a builder who loves to ship: pragmatic on trade-offs, careful on quality. You move fast, but fast does not mean sloppy.

  • You care about correctness, reliability, security, and long-term maintainability, and you leave codebases and teams better than you found them.

  • You are curious about how investment decisions are made and want to understand the data behind them, not just move it.

  • You see AI-powered development as a competitive advantage, not a novelty, and use agentic AI as a core part of how you work.

  • You communicate clearly on progress, trade-offs, and risk, and you own problems end-to-end.


What we offer

  • Work with petabytes of data and the most cutting-edge tools in and beyond asset management, with Day 1 ownership of challenging, varied work and a steep learning curve.

  • Become part of a unique success story in European asset management, alongside the most knowledgeable experts in the industry on one of the most consequential investment themes of the next decade.

  • A motivated, highly international team (15 nationalities) that gathers in person at our Berlin HQ and supports each other, with flat hierarchies and direct interaction with our management team and investors.

  • Visa sponsorship, relocation support, and a competitive compensation package with a meaningful variable component tied to fund performance.

description:
About 3E:

3E is a mission-driven company dedicated to creating a safer and more sustainable world. We offer award-winning regulatory intelligence and AI solutions to help organizations protect people and products. With over 35 years of experience and a global presence, we empower our customers with innovative compliance solutions. 

You will get to work at a company that combines startup agility with the stability of an industry leader. Partner with enterprise customers and global experts to advance environmental safety and solve complex data science challenges.

Join us and make an impact!

About the Role

As an Implementation Project Manager at 3E, you’ll lead larger, more complex customer implementations where successful delivery requires multiple products, technical contributors, workstreams, dependencies, and stakeholders to operate against one coordinated plan.

You’ll be accountable for turning the customer’s scope of work into an executable implementation strategy and for determining whether the overall project succeeds—on time, within scope, adopted, and connected to a clear customer outcome. You’ll establish success and acceptance criteria, own the integrated project plan, manage risk and change, coordinate specialists and technical teams, and give both customers and 3E leadership a clear, data-backed view of project health.

You’ll understand the technical delivery deeply enough to challenge assumptions, identify dependencies, connect customer needs with the right specialists, and engage credibly with Product and Engineering. You won’t need to personally execute every configuration, migration, or integration; your role is to ensure those pieces come together into a successful customer outcome.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead complex new-logo, cross-sell, and Value Realization implementations from internal handoff through customer acceptance and formal close.

  • Translate complex scopes of work into an integrated delivery strategy covering products, workstreams, milestones, resources, dependencies, assumptions, exclusions, and acceptance criteria.

  • Lead technical discovery and pre-integration planning with customers, CX technical specialists, and relevant internal teams.

  • Own the master implementation plan and coordinate implementation specialists, Product, Engineering, Data, Cloud, technical consultants, external partners, and customer resources.

  • Establish measurable success and acceptance criteria at kickoff and maintain accountability for those outcomes throughout delivery.

  • Lead customer project governance, including senior stakeholder and sponsor communications.

  • Maintain the milestone tracker and conduct phase-gate reviews, giving a clear assessment of whether projects are on track, at risk, or behind and establishing mitigation plans when required.

  • Identify cross-workstream dependencies and risks early and determine their impact on the critical path.

  • Lead complex, multi-product delivery by managing scope and change control, coordinating custom development through launch, maintaining a unified customer plan across teams, and providing leadership with clear, data-backed reporting on project health, risk, timelines, value, and adoption.

  • Build and maintain dashboards or reporting tools that make project status and risks visible without relying solely on status meetings.

  • Lead customer escalations diplomatically while maintaining accountability for customer commitments, decisions, resources, data readiness, and signoffs.

  • Partner with Commercial on implementation handoff and identify expansion opportunities or renewal risks surfaced during delivery.

  • Represent the delivery perspective during pre-sales scoping of complex or higher-risk opportunities so commitments can be successfully delivered.

  • Drive structured post-onboarding Value Realization Projects, including complex migrations, integrations, optimization, remediation, and workflow initiatives.

  • Manage multiple concurrent implementations and make prioritization decisions based on risk, complexity, dependencies, and customer impact.

  • Identify opportunities to improve implementation processes, delivery predictability, time-to-value, and the overall customer experience.

What Makes You a Great Fit

Required

  • 3–5 years of experience in software implementation, customer onboarding, technical account or project management, or professional services, ideally within B2B SaaS, technology, or information services.

  • Demonstrated experience leading complex customer implementations with multiple workstreams, technical dependencies, contributors, or products.

  • Experience owning project scope, plans, milestones, risks, dependencies, change control, customer communication, and delivery outcomes.

  • Strong technical aptitude and the ability to understand configuration, data, integration, and technical delivery sufficiently to coordinate specialists and identify risk; coding is not required.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead customer conversations and communicate credibly with senior customer stakeholders.

  • Ability to lead and influence cross-functional contributors without formal authority.

  • Experience managing multiple concurrent projects and making informed prioritization decisions based on customer and business impact.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, analytical thinking, judgment, and problem-solving skills.

  • Proficiency with CRM tools such as Salesforce or HubSpot and Microsoft Office, with comfort using data, dashboards, and systems of record to communicate project health.

  • Ability to navigate ambiguity and changing scope while maintaining accountability for outcomes.

  • Willingness to travel 10–20%.

title: Senior IT Analyst
description:
About The Role

The Senior IT Analyst is the principal in-house resource responsible for day-to-day IT support, providing first and second-line user support and day-to-day IT operations for approximately 80 users. As the principal person responsible for day-to-day IT operations, they will take ownership of incidents and service requests across the support lifecycle rather than operating solely as an escalation resource.
 
This is a broad, senior analyst role for someone who is technically capable, comfortable working independently and able to manage competing priorities. The postholder will respond directly to users, resolve routine enquiries and requests, investigate more complex issues through to resolution and coordinate external technology suppliers where specialist expertise is needed. Alongside business-as-usual responsibilities, the role will support and deliver smaller technology projects and service improvements.
 
By keeping FAIRR’s technology secure, reliable and easy to use, the role enables colleagues to focus on delivering FAIRR’s mission with investors and partners worldwide.


Key Outcomes & Accountabilities

OUTCOME 1: Users receive dependable, responsive IT support, with issues owned and resolved end to end

  • Act as the principal in-house point of contact for day-to-day IT support, providing both first and second-line assistance according to operational needs.
  • Resolve straightforward incidents and requests promptly, while taking the lead on more complex technical issues requiring deeper investigation and second-line expertise.
  • Own and manage incidents and service requests from initial contact through to resolution, including access, software, equipment, permissions and non-standard user requirements, coordinating third-party suppliers or specialist support when required.
  • Monitor recurring issues, identify root causes and implement practical improvements to reduce repeat incidents.
  • Maintain accurate support records and produce clear information on service volumes, performance, trends and user experience.
 
OUTCOME 2: Joiners, movers and leavers have the right access and equipment at the right time, and no more
  • Coordinate all IT activities for joiners, movers and leavers in collaboration with HR and relevant managers.
  • Create, amend and remove user accounts, licences, group memberships, permissions and application access accurately and on time, including removal of leaver access no later than the end of their last working day (or earlier where instructed by P&C).
  • Prepare, issue, recover and securely manage laptops, mobile devices, peripherals and other IT equipment.
  • Perform periodic access reviews and maintain appropriate evidence of approvals and completed actions.
  • Manage shared, service and other non-person accounts, ensuring ownership, purpose and access are recorded.
  • Where instructed by P&C or the Senior IT Manager, securely preserve or retrieve account and device data to support subject access requests, investigations or legal matters, maintaining confidentiality throughout.
 
OUTCOME 3: IT changes are implemented in a controlled way with minimal disruption
  • Plan, assess, document, communicate and implement routine IT changes in a controlled manner.
  • Ensure changes have appropriate approvals, testing, implementation steps, back-out arrangements and post-change review where proportionate.
  • Maintain the IT change schedule and coordinate activities to minimise disruption to users and business operations.
  • Communicate planned changes clearly to affected users and stakeholders.
  • Where changes need to take place outside normal working hours, schedule these in advance with the Senior IT Manager’s agreement (see Section 8).
 
OUTCOME 4: IT services and workplace technology operate reliably and are used effectively and securely
  • Administer Microsoft 365 and other cloud applications used by the organisation, including routine configuration, licence and user administration.
  • Support laptops, mobile devices, meeting-room technology, printers, connectivity and standard workplace applications.
  • Coordinate hardware repairs, replacements, warranty cases, software renewals and operational supplier activities.
  • Maintain user guides, knowledge articles, standard operating procedures and support documentation.
  • Provide practical guidance and training that helps users make effective and secure use of technology.
 
OUTCOME 5: IT records, controls and evidence are complete, current and audit-ready
  • Maintain complete and accurate asset, software, licence, supplier and other operational IT registers.
  • Record equipment allocation, ownership, status, location, lifecycle and disposal information, and perform periodic reconciliations.
  • Follow and help maintain IT policies, standards, procedures and control evidence.
  • Complete routine operational checks and scheduled control activities, escalating risks, exceptions or control failures promptly.
  • Support audits, reviews and compliance activities by providing accurate records and evidence.
  • Handle devices, accounts and information in line with security, privacy and records-management requirements.
  • Support compliance with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 (as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025), including immediately escalating any suspected personal data breach to the Data Protection Lead so that the organisation can meet the 72-hour ICO reporting deadline where applicable.
 
OUTCOME 6: Small projects and improvements are delivered and technology keeps getting better
  • Deliver or support small IT projects, upgrades, application roll-outs and service improvements.
  • Gather requirements, coordinate suppliers, plan user communications, support testing and manage implementation activities.
  • Identify opportunities to improve reliability, security, efficiency and the user experience.
  • Keep project actions, risks, decisions, documentation and handover materials up to date.


Success Measures

Success in the role will be assessed through:
 
Service delivery

  • Users receive dependable and responsive first and second-line technical support, with routine and complex issues resolved effectively.
  • Incidents and requests are responded to and resolved within agreed service levels.
  • User satisfaction with IT support is consistently positive.
Accuracy, security and control
  • Incidents, requests, access changes and joiner, mover and leaver activities are completed accurately and on time.
  • 100% of leaver accounts disabled by the end of the last working day; new joiners fully equipped and set up on day one.
  • Operational records, registers and control evidence are complete, current and reliable.
  • Periodic access reviews and asset reconciliations completed on schedule with no significant audit findings.
Change and improvement
  • Changes and small projects are delivered in a controlled way with minimal disruption.
  • Recurring problems are reduced and practical improvements are implemented continuously.
  • Feedback from the Senior IT Manager, colleagues and suppliers on collaboration, communication and ownership.


Technical Expertise & Role-Specific Capability

Essential

  • Strong hands-on experience providing both first and second-line IT support within a modern workplace environment, with particular strength in diagnosing and resolving more complex technical issues.
  • Demonstrable experience managing a broad range of incidents and service requests through their full lifecycle, from initial user contact to resolution.
  • Practical experience of joiner, mover and leaver processes, identity administration, permissions and access control.
  • Experience administering Microsoft 365 and supporting Windows devices, laptops, mobile devices and common business applications.
  • Experience maintaining IT asset records, operational registers, procedures and control evidence.
  • Understanding of proportionate change management, information security and data protection practices.
  • Ability to troubleshoot methodically, make sound decisions and know when to engage specialist support.
  • Experience coordinating external IT suppliers and seeing actions through to completion.
  • Ability to organise a varied workload independently and balance urgent support needs with planned operational work.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical matters to non-technical users.
  • Experience contributing to or delivering small IT projects and technology changes.
 
Desirable
  • Experience in a small organisation where the role covers a broad range of operational IT responsibilities.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, Autopilot, SharePoint and Teams administration.
  • Experience with IT service management tools and ITIL-aligned working practices.
  • Experience supporting SaaS applications and coordinating managed service, cyber security or other specialist partners.
  • Relevant technical or service management certification (e.g. Microsoft 365 / Azure certifications, ITIL Foundation), or equivalent practical experience.


Career Framework Expectations

Our Career Framework provides a shared approach to development and performance across the organisation. It is built around four core pillars: Connect, Deliver, Focus and Lead, which outline the key behaviours and expectations expected at all levels.
In this role, the pillars look like this:

CONNECT — Building trust, relationships and collaboration

  • Collaborative and able to build effective relationships with users, colleagues and suppliers.
  • Technically credible, user-focused and committed to providing a high-quality service.
DELIVER — Driving outcomes and execution
  • Proactive and self-sufficient, with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
  • Calm and organised when handling competing priorities or service disruption.
FOCUS — Applying expertise and driving improvement
  • Detail-oriented and disciplined about keeping records, documentation and actions up to date.
  • Curious and improvement-minded, with a willingness to learn and adapt.
LEAD — Leading self, others and organisational success
  • Practical and proportionate, applying appropriate control without unnecessary bureaucracy.
  • Role-models secure and responsible use of technology and shares knowledge so colleagues become more self-sufficient.


Organisational Values

  1. We are change makers: keeps the technology behind FAIRR’s work dependable, so colleagues can spend their time on the mission rather than on IT problems.
  2. We collaborate: works closely with HR, managers, colleagues and suppliers to deliver a joined-up service.
  3. We innovate: looks for better, simpler and more secure ways of working, and delivers improvements that last.
  4. We act with integrity: handles privileged access, devices and personal data responsibly, confidentially and transparently.


Additional Information

Working Arrangements
Hybrid working from near Marble Arch (Oxford Street), London, UK, in line with FAIRR’s organisational working arrangements.
 
Normal working hours are 9.00am–5.30pm, Monday to Friday. Because much of the role is hands-on (devices, meeting-room technology, joiner set-up), the postholder will be expected to work on site at least 3 days per week and on key operational days such as new starter inductions.
 
Occasional work outside normal hours may be required for planned changes or urgent incidents. This will be agreed in advance wherever possible and recognised through time off in lieu in line with FAIRR policy.

Travel Requirements
Occasional travel within London and the UK may be required (e.g. supplier visits, training or events). International travel is not an expected part of the role.

Salary Range
To be confirmed during recruitment stage.

Benefits
Benefits will be provided in line with FAIRR’s standard employee benefits package.

Pre-Employment Checks
Appointment is subject to proof of the right to work in the UK, satisfactory references and, because the role holds privileged system access, a Basic DBS criminal record check. Information will be handled in line with the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and data protection law.
 
Equal Opportunities & Reasonable Adjustments
FAIRR welcomes applications from all backgrounds. If you need any adjustments during the recruitment process or in the role, please let us know.

Performance & Flexibility

  • This JD forms the basis for performance reviews.
  • Performance against this JD will be reviewed during the 5-month probationary period and in regular one-to-ones thereafter.
  • This job description is not exhaustive or contractual. The organisation reserves the right to modify duties and responsibilities to reflect organisational needs, subject to consultation where appropriate.

About the role

We’re looking for a Financial Crime Framework & Innovation Manager to lead our KYC Framework & Controls team in Pleo’s first line of defence. The team owns our financial crime framework across the UK and EU/EEA, covering KYC, AML/CFT and sanctions screening. You’ll lead a team of specialists while staying hands-on, owning change end to end across multiple entities and jurisdictions. Compliance is a given; the bigger opportunity is using AI and technology to cut manual effort and sharpen our controls. We welcome all backgrounds, so apply even if you don’t tick every box.

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

You’ll report to our DK/EEA MLRO and lead a remote team of five financial crime specialists. You’ll partner with Operations, who run our KYC processes, plus Product, Engineering, Legal, Compliance and our separate transaction monitoring team.

What you’ll be doing

As a Financial Crime Framework & Innovation Manager, you will:

  • Own and evolve Pleo’s financial crime framework for KYC, AML/CFT and sanctions screening across the UK and EU/EEA

  • Lead and support a remote team of specialists, building trust and a real sense of team

  • Drive change end to end, from spotting the gap to embedding the fix with Operations

  • Use automation and AI to reduce manual effort and improve decision quality

  • Lead our move to a new screening vendor through to go-live

  • Shape our readiness for the EU AML Regulation

  • Manage regulatory audits and inspections, and help set the team’s annual strategy

On the roadmap: the screening vendor migration (go-live planned for Q1) and the EU AML Regulation, which applies from July 2027. We’re also finalising a new financial crime operating model, so some responsibilities may shift.

What you bring


You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

  • Significant experience designing and improving financial crime frameworks, controls and operating models in the UK or EU

  • Experience across multiple entities and jurisdictions, covering UK and EU/EEA requirements

  • Experience managing specialists while staying hands-on

  • A track record of leading change end to end, from stakeholders to delivery

  • Demonstrable experience driving innovation, for example AI-enabled workflows or automated controls

  • The ability to turn complex financial crime concepts into clear, practical guidance

It’s a bonus if you have:

  • Led a screening vendor migration or a similar system implementation

  • Hands-on experience preparing for the EU AML Regulation

You might come from a fintech or a bank. If you’re from a larger bank, show us where you’ve owned broad scope.

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

  • You lead specialists by building trust and giving them room

  • You’d rather lead an office-based team. Yours is fully remote, and connection takes deliberate effort

How you’ll develop in this role

In your first six months at Pleo, you’ll:

  • Take ownership of the screening vendor migration and lead it through go-live

  • Take day-to-day ownership of the EU AML Regulation programme

  • Bring your remote team closer together

title: Senior Software Engineer, Canvas Core
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Canvas Core team builds and maintains the foundational platform that powers Mural’s visual thinking experience. This includes the infinite canvas, key editor components, document editing behaviors, asset management, real-time collaboration, and the systems that enable fast, reliable, and intuitive interaction on the canvas.

We’re also responsible for the Mural UI, the real-time message protocol that enables seamless remote collaboration, and the developer-friendly APIs that internal teams use to build features like diagramming, workshops, presentations, integrations, and AI-enabled product capabilities.

Our mission is to ensure the Mural editor is fast, reliable, intuitive, and easy to build on.

We prioritize performance, simplicity, developer experience, and platform quality, enabling teams across the company to ship quickly and safely on top of Canvas Core.

YOUR MISSION

As a Senior Software Engineer, you’ll help design, build, and improve the Canvas platform so that the Mural editor remains reliable, high-performing, and intuitive for our users.

You’ll work on the systems that power real-time collaboration, shared document editing, spatial interactions, rendering and interaction performance, asset management, developer APIs, and AI-enabled product capabilities across the Mural editor.

Your role will be to reduce platform complexity, improve the quality and speed of Canvas development, and help teams ship high-quality editor experiences quickly and safely. You’ll partner closely with Product, Design, Engineering, and other stakeholders to turn ambiguous product and platform problems into clear, maintainable technical solutions.

Senior Engineers at Mural lead by example through strong technical execution, thoughtful design, high-quality implementation, and collaborative problem-solving. They help raise the bar for their team through design discussions, code reviews, mentoring, documentation, and pragmatic improvements to engineering practices.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own and deliver new Canvas platform capabilities and improvements from problem definition through implementation, release, measurement, and iteration

  • Partner with Product and Design to shape high-quality user experiences, balancing pragmatic technical delivery with long-term platform needs

  • Design and build maintainable Canvas platform systems, with accountability for quality, performance, reliability, and developer experience

title: Head of PMO
description:
About Us

 

Plentific is a property technology platform used by housing providers, local authorities, housing associations, asset managers, and contractors across the UK and Germany to manage repairs, maintenance, compliance, and contractor operations at scale. Our platform combines marketplace infrastructure, workflow software, automation, and operational analytics. It is designed for the complexity, volume, and regulatory demands of social housing, public sector property portfolios, and large residential operations. We are headquartered in London, with engineering and operations across the UK and Germany. We are growing the team to expand the platform's coverage across Europe and to integrate AI throughout the product and operating model. If you want to work on hard, real-world problems in the world's largest asset class, we would like to hear from you.


Role purpose

Plentific is standing up a Controlling PMO: a function with the mandate to set and enforce common delivery standards, hold a single, current view of the whole portfolio, and work directly with senior management to unblock the issues that put individual projects’ targets at risk. The PMO Lead owns this function day to day — coaching Programme and Project Managers (PMs) to a consistently high standard, building the portfolio-level reporting that gives leadership real visibility, and acting as the bridge between delivery teams and senior management when a decision or an unblock is needed.

This is a hands-on, first-of-its-kind role at Plentific: the PMO Lead will stand up the standards, cadence, and reporting described below largely from scratch, and will be judged on how quickly the portfolio becomes visible, consistent, and genuinely governed as a result.


Key responsibilities

1. Coach Programme & Project Managers, and hold the standard

  • Own and continuously improve the standard toolkit every programme uses — charter, RAID log, status report, change log.

  • Coach PMs on using the standards well — raising the general standard of programme management practice, not just chasing form-filling.

  • Own the stage-gate review process: assess whether a programme is genuinely ready to pass each gate, and issue go/no-go sign-off.

  • Set and enforce mandatory reporting — PMs submit standard, current status on a fixed cadence; the PMO follows up where reporting lapses.

2. Build and run portfolio-level reporting and governance

  • Consolidate individual programme status into one current, accurate portfolio view of schedule, spend, risk, and resourcing.

  • Own the portfolio tracker and the cadence of updates that feed it.

  • Track cross-programme risks and dependencies; make sure each has a named owner and a clear escalation threshold.

  • Prepare and present the portfolio report at each Steering Committee review.

  • Track benefits realisation — confirm delivered programmes actually produced the outcome they were funded for.

3. Work with senior management to report and unblock

  • Act as the primary escalation point when a programme risk or dependency needs a decision above the PM’s authority.

  • Bring blockers to the right senior stakeholder quickly, with a clear ask and options — not just a status update.

  • Represent delivery status and risk to senior management accurately and without spin, including when the news is difficult.

  • Chair or co-chair the portfolio review, and prepare materials for Steering Committee meetings.

  • Track follow-through on decisions and unblocks agreed with senior management, so they don’t silently drop.


Authority and mandate

This role carries a Controlling PMO mandate — meaning the successful candidate has the authority to require compliance, not just recommend it:

  • Authority, via the PMO charter, to require compliance with standards and mandatory reporting across all active programmes.

  • Owns sign-off at stage gates — a programme cannot proceed to the next phase without PMO gate approval.

  • Is the named escalation path for cross-programme risk and resourcing conflicts.

  • Does not directly manage PMs day to day: PMs remain people-managed within their business unit, with a functional (“dotted-line”) reporting relationship into the PMO for delivery standards, gate compliance, and escalation.


Key relationships

  • Executive Sponsor / Steering Committee — monthly portfolio reporting, escalation, gate decisions.

  • Programme & Project Managers — coaching, mandatory reporting, gate reviews.

  • Senior management / business leaders — status reporting, unblocking, resourcing conversations.

  • PMO Analyst (future hire) — as the portfolio grows, this role would oversee a second PMO hire supporting reporting and gate reviews.


How success is measured

  • On-time delivery rate across active programmes.

  • Forecast accuracy — how closely planned cost and effort track actuals over time.

  • Share of active programmes with an up-to-date RAID log.

  • Time from a risk being raised to being escalated to someone who can unblock it.

  • Sponsor and PM confidence in delivery, tracked each quarter.


Person specification

Essential

  • Proven experience running programme or project governance, ideally in a PMO capacity, in a fast-moving organisation.

  • Comfortable holding people accountable to standards without owning their day-to-day work — a coaching style, not a command style.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills; credible in the room with senior leadership.

  • Confident synthesising status across multiple concurrent initiatives into a single, honest, current view.

  • A clear, direct communicator, comfortable surfacing bad news early rather than letting it surface late.

Desirable

  • A formal programme/PMO qualification (e.g. P3O, PRINCE2, MSP, PMP).

  • Experience standing up a PMO from scratch, or maturing one from a Supportive to a Controlling model.

  • Familiarity with portfolio/PPM reporting tools.

Benefits

 

As you can see, we are quickly progressing with our ambitious plans and are eager to grow our team of doers to achieve our vision of managing over 2 million properties through our platform across various countries. You can help us shape the future of property management across the globe. Here’s what we offer:
